sop_modules.name: Deck Protection & Furniture Staging
sop_modules.description: Mask siding at ledger board junction, deploy landscape and hardscape protection, stage deck furniture off work area, mask deck-mounted light fixtures. Siding protection upgrades to full plastic sheeting for spray_backbrush method.

tasks.name: Siding Protection at Ledger Board
tasks.description: Mask and tape siding adjacent to deck at ledger board junction where stain may splash or overspray. Tape blue masking tape at siding-to-deck transition, then hang plastic sheeting 4-6 ft up siding face. Light tape for brush application, full plastic sheet for spray_backbrush.

quality_notes.all: Tape at siding-to-deck transition line. Secure plastic sheeting against wind. For spray_backbrush, extend plastic 4-6 ft up siding face to contain overspray drift.

tasks.name: Below-Deck Landscape Protection
tasks.description: Deploy plastic sheeting over plantings and landscape below elevated deck. Stain drips through deck board gaps onto vegetation below. 4-6 mil plastic minimum. Secure with landscape stakes or weights.

quality_notes.all: Full coverage of vegetation below deck. Stain drips through board gaps — protection is mandatory for elevated decks regardless of application method.

tasks.name: Adjacent Hardscape Protection
tasks.description: Deploy canvas drop cloths and plastic over patio, walkway, or driveway adjacent to deck at grade level. Protect from stain overspray, drip, and foot traffic tracking.

quality_notes.all: Canvas for crew traffic areas (non-slip). Extend coverage to overspray zone for spray_backbrush. Tape edges to prevent wind lift.

tasks.name: Deck Furniture Staging
tasks.description: Move deck furniture, planters, grills, and accessories to staging area off deck surface. All items must be removed from work area before prep or application. Count as furniture groups (table+chairs = 1 group).

quality_notes.all: Stage furniture to covered area or garage if available. Cover with tarps if staging outdoors. Document pre-existing furniture condition.

tasks.name: Deck Light Fixture Masking
tasks.description: Mask deck-mounted and railing-mounted light fixtures with tape and plastic bags. Disconnect power if accessible. Conditional — only when fixtures are present on deck.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage of fixture body and lens. Secure tape and plastic against wind. Do not block path lighting if working over multiple days.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Siding protection first -> Landscape/hardscape protection -> Furniture staging -> Fixture masking last.

sop_modules.name: Deck Floor Surface Preparation
sop_modules.description: Floor-specific prep sequence: moisture content verification (mandatory hard stop), seasoning check (new PT pine only), mill glaze sanding (new milled wood only), refinishing sand (previously coated only), pressure wash, and mildew treatment (conditional). Task activation driven by wood_condition and substrate_type dimensions.

tasks.name: Moisture Content Verification
tasks.description: Test deck wood moisture content with pin-type moisture meter. MC must read <=15% before any stain application. Test multiple locations across deck field — shaded areas and end grain read higher. MC >15% is a HARD STOP — do not stain. Retest after 24 hr dry period if initial test fails.

quality_notes.all: Test minimum 5 locations distributed across deck. Include shaded areas and areas near ground contact. Document all readings. MC >15% = hard stop, do not proceed.

tasks.name: PT Pine Seasoning Verification
tasks.description: Verify pressure-treated pine has seasoned minimum 3 months from install date before staining. PT lumber is kiln-dried after treatment but retains chemical preservatives that inhibit stain absorption. Less than 3 months = HARD STOP. Verify install date from construction schedule or GC.

quality_notes.all: Document install date. Water drop test: if water beads on wood surface, PT chemicals are still too concentrated — wood needs more seasoning time. Water should absorb within 10 seconds.

tasks.name: Mill Glaze Removal Sanding
tasks.description: Sand new milled wood deck boards with 60-grit to remove mill glaze (burnished surface from planer). Mill glaze prevents stain penetration. Sand with grain direction. Random orbital sander or belt sander for floor field. Applies to new milled (non-rough-sawn) lumber only.

quality_notes.all: Sand entire floor field with 60-grit. Sand WITH grain direction only — cross-grain scratches telegraph through semi-transparent stain. Water drop test after sanding: water should absorb within 5 seconds. If water beads, sand further.

tasks.name: Deck Floor Refinishing Sand
tasks.description: Sand previously coated deck floor with 80-100 grit to remove failing coating, roughen surface, and promote adhesion for new stain. For solid stain over solid stain: degloss and feather edges of peeling areas. For penetrating stain over penetrating: lighter scuff is sufficient.

quality_notes.all: 80-grit for solid stain removal, 100-grit for scuffing penetrating stain residue. Focus on high-traffic wear areas and peeling edges. Vacuum dust before washing.

tasks.name: Pressure Wash Deck Floor
tasks.description: Pressure wash deck floor field at 1,500-2,000 PSI. Use fan tip (25-40 degree) to avoid gouging wood. Maintain consistent distance (12-18 inches from surface). Work WITH grain direction. Allow 24-48 hr dry time before staining. Verify MC <=15% after drying.

quality_notes.all: Fan tip only — never use zero-degree or turbo tip on wood. Maintain consistent distance to avoid gouging or furrowing. Work in consistent overlapping passes WITH grain. 24-48 hr dry time minimum before staining.

tasks.name: Mildew Eradication Treatment
tasks.description: Apply mildew treatment solution (sodium hypochlorite/oxygen bleach) to mildew-affected areas. Allow 10-15 min dwell time. Scrub with stiff bristle brush. Rinse thoroughly with pressure washer. Mildew must be killed before staining — stain over mildew will fail within one season.

quality_notes.all: Identify mildew vs dirt: apply bleach to suspect area — mildew lightens, dirt does not. Kill ALL mildew before proceeding. Rinse thoroughly — bleach residue inhibits stain adhesion.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Moisture test (hard stop) -> Seasoning verify (new PT pine, hard stop) -> Mill glaze sand (new) OR refinishing sand (previously coated) -> Mildew treatment (conditional) -> Pressure wash (all) -> 24-48 hr dry time -> Re-verify MC <=15%.

sop_modules.name: Deck Railing & Spindle Preparation
sop_modules.description: Railing-specific prep: hand sand railings and spindles, clean railing surfaces. Activated when scope_components includes railings (floor_and_railings or full_deck).

tasks.name: Railing Hand Sand
tasks.description: Hand sand railings (top rail, bottom rail, posts) with 80-100 grit. Remove mill glaze on new wood or scuff existing finish on previously coated. Sand all faces — top, sides, and underside of cap rail.

quality_notes.all: Hand sand all accessible faces. Pay attention to cap rail top (horizontal wear surface). Sand WITH grain. Vacuum or brush dust before washing.

tasks.name: Spindle Hand Sand
tasks.description: Hand sand individual spindles/balusters with 100-grit. All 4 sides plus top and bottom joints. Turned spindles require contour sanding with flexible sandpaper. High labor intensity — ~2-3 min per square spindle, 4-5 min per turned spindle.

quality_notes.all: Sand all faces including top/bottom joints where spindle meets rail. Turned spindles: wrap sandpaper around profile and work with rotation. Remove all dust before washing.

tasks.name: Railing and Spindle Cleaning
tasks.description: Clean railing system by hand wash or low-pressure rinse (500-800 PSI max on railing components). Remove sanding dust, dirt, and debris. Do NOT use full-pressure wash on spindles — can damage turned profiles and loosen joints.

quality_notes.all: Low pressure or hand wash for railing components. Spindles especially — high pressure can loosen connections. Allow same dry time as floor before staining.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Railing sand -> Spindle sand -> Railing/spindle wash -> 24-48 hr dry time with floor.

sop_modules.name: Chemical Wood Restoration (Weathered Deck)
sop_modules.description: Three-step chemical restoration for weathered wood: (1) alkaline strip/clean to remove gray oxidation, failed coating residue, and open wood pores, (2) acid brighten with oxalic acid to restore natural color and neutralize alkaline residue, (3) rinse and verify drying. Cedar/redwood auto-add brightener even without full strip. Effectively a separate mobilization day — 24-48 hr dry time required after final rinse before staining.

tasks.name: Alkaline Stripper Application
tasks.description: Apply sodium percarbonate or sodium hydroxide-based deck cleaner/stripper to weathered wood surface. Spray application with pump sprayer or airless at low pressure. Work in manageable sections (100-200 SF) to control dwell time. Keep surface wet — do not allow stripper to dry on wood.

quality_notes.all: Work in sections. Keep surface wet — dried stripper causes blotching. Protect adjacent landscaping from chemical runoff. PPE required: gloves, eye protection, boots.

tasks.name: Stripper Dwell Time
tasks.description: Allow alkaline stripper to dwell 15-20 minutes per section. Monitor — do not allow to dry. Reapply if surface begins drying before dwell time is complete. Dwell time is critical for breaking down gray oxidation layer and opening wood pores.

quality_notes.all: 15-20 min dwell. Monitor temperature — hot sun shortens dwell time (chemical evaporates faster). Overcast/cool conditions are ideal for chemical restoration.

tasks.name: Stripper Agitation/Scrub
tasks.description: Agitate stripper with stiff bristle brush or floor scrubber after dwell time. Work WITH grain direction. Scrubbing mechanically assists chemical breakdown of failed coating and gray oxidation layer.

quality_notes.all: Scrub WITH grain. Stiff synthetic bristle — do NOT use wire brush (embeds metal particles that cause rust stains). Focus on areas with heavy gray oxidation or coating residue.

tasks.name: Pressure Rinse After Strip
tasks.description: Pressure rinse stripped deck surface at 1,500-2,000 PSI to remove stripper residue, loosened coating, and oxidation debris. Thorough rinse is critical — alkaline residue left on wood will interfere with acid brightener step.

quality_notes.all: Thorough rinse — run-off should be clear, not brown/gray. Work WITH grain. Fan tip (25-40 degree) at 12-18 inch distance.

tasks.name: Acid Brightener Application
tasks.description: Apply oxalic acid wood brightener to stripped deck surface. Brightener neutralizes alkaline stripper residue, restores natural wood color (removes tannin surface deposits on cedar/redwood), and lowers wood pH to optimal range for stain absorption. Apply with pump sprayer.

quality_notes.all: Even application. Keep surface wet. Oxalic acid is especially critical for cedar/redwood — dissolves tannin deposits that cause bleed-through. PPE required: gloves, eye protection.

tasks.name: Brightener Dwell Time
tasks.description: Allow acid brightener to dwell 10-15 minutes. Wood should visibly lighten and return toward natural color. Do not allow to dry on surface. Shorter dwell time than stripper — acid works faster.

quality_notes.all: 10-15 min dwell. Visual check: wood should lighten noticeably. If wood does not lighten, second application may be needed (rare on standard weathering).

tasks.name: Final Rinse After Brightener
tasks.description: Pressure rinse brightened deck surface at 1,000-1,500 PSI (lower pressure than strip rinse — wood is now clean and open-pored). Remove all acid residue. This is the final wet step before drying period.

quality_notes.all: Lower pressure than strip rinse — wood pores are open and vulnerable. Gentle thorough rinse. Run-off should be clear. No chemical residue remaining.

tasks.name: Post-Restoration Dry Verification
tasks.description: Verify deck has dried 24-48 hours after final rinse before proceeding to stain application. Pin-type moisture meter must read MC <=15%. Chemical restoration opens wood pores, so drying may take longer than standard wash. Do not stain if MC >15%.

quality_notes.all: 24-48 hr minimum dry time. Test multiple locations including shaded areas. MC <=15% is hard stop. Chemical restoration opens pores — wood absorbs more water and takes longer to dry. Plan for separate mobilization day.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: STRICT SEQUENCE: Strip apply -> Strip dwell (15-20 min) -> Strip scrub -> Strip rinse -> Brighten apply -> Brighten dwell (10-15 min) -> Brighten rinse -> 24-48 hr dry -> MC verify. Cedar/redwood: brightener is mandatory even as standalone tannin treatment (without strip).

sop_modules.name: Deck Floor Stain Application
sop_modules.description: Apply stain to deck floor field surface. Application method selection: spray_backbrush (primary, fastest), brush (traditional), pad (smooth floor application), roll (alternative). Back-brushing is mandatory when spraying penetrating stain — forces stain into wood grain pores. Second coat conditional on coating_type: semi_solid and solid_stain require 2 coats; clear_sealer and semi_transparent are typically 1 coat (2 coat optional).

tasks.name: Floor Stain — Spray + Back-Brush
tasks.description: Spray stain onto deck floor with airless sprayer at low pressure (800-1,200 PSI), immediately follow with stiff bristle brush to work stain into wood grain. Two-person operation: one sprays, one follows with brush. Work in 3-4 board widths. Maintain wet edge. Back-brushing is MANDATORY — spray-only is prohibited for penetrating stains.

quality_notes.all: Low pressure spray — avoid atomizing stain. Back-brush immediately (within 2-3 minutes of spray). Work WITH grain. Maintain wet edge across full deck width. Do not allow puddles — penetrating stain must absorb, not pool.

tasks.name: Floor Stain — Brush Application
tasks.description: Apply stain to deck floor by brush. 4-6 inch stiff synthetic bristle brush. Work stain into grain with firm pressure. Work 2-3 board widths at a time. Maintain wet edge. Slower than spray_backbrush but provides maximum control and grain penetration.

quality_notes.all: Firm brush pressure to work stain into grain. WITH grain direction. 2-3 board widths per pass. Maintain wet edge. No puddles — wipe excess immediately.

tasks.name: Floor Stain — Pad Applicator
tasks.description: Apply stain to deck floor with pad/lamb's wool applicator on extension pole. Smooth, even application for large flat surfaces. Best for semi-transparent and clear sealers on smooth-surface boards. Not suitable for rough-sawn lumber.

quality_notes.all: Even, thin coats. Pad applicator delivers uniform coverage on smooth boards. Work WITH grain. Replace pad when saturated — worn pads leave uneven stain.

tasks.name: Floor Stain — Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply stain to deck floor with roller (3/8 inch nap for smooth boards, 1/2 inch for rough-sawn). Back-brush recommended after rolling to work stain into grain. Extension pole for ergonomic application.

quality_notes.all: Thin even coats. Back-brush after rolling is recommended for penetrating stains. Do not over-apply — penetrating stain that pools will not absorb and will become tacky.

tasks.name: Floor Stain — Second Coat
tasks.description: Apply second coat of stain to deck floor. Required for semi_solid and solid_stain coating types. Same application method as coat 1. Allow minimum recoat time per product TDS (typically 4-24 hr for penetrating, 4 hr for solid). For penetrating stains: second coat may not absorb fully — wipe excess after 15-20 min if stain does not penetrate.

quality_notes.all: Same method as coat 1. Verify recoat time per TDS. For semi_solid: second coat may partially absorb — wipe excess if not absorbed after 20 min. For solid_stain: even coverage, maintain wet edge, no runs or sags.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: One application method task active per project (spray_backbrush OR brush OR pad OR roll). Coat 2 conditional on coating_type. Allow recoat time between coats per product TDS.

sop_modules.name: Deck Railing & Spindle Stain Application
sop_modules.description: Apply stain to railing system (top rail, bottom rail, posts) and individual spindles/balusters. Brush is primary method for railings and spindles. Spray_backbrush for long railing runs. Spindles are always brushed individually regardless of railing method. Second coat conditional on coating_type (semi_solid and solid_stain).

tasks.name: Railing Stain — Spray + Back-Brush
tasks.description: Spray stain onto railing system (top rail, bottom rail, posts) with airless at low pressure, immediately back-brush to work into grain. Efficient for long railing runs. Shield siding and floor from overspray. Two-person operation.

quality_notes.all: Low pressure to minimize overspray on railing components. Back-brush all faces immediately. Shield adjacent siding with cardboard or plastic.

tasks.name: Railing Stain — Brush Application
tasks.description: Apply stain to railing system by brush. 2-3 inch detail brush for posts and rail faces. Work stain into all faces: top, sides, underside of cap rail, post faces. Primary method for railing components.

quality_notes.all: Stain all faces of railing components. Cap rail top is critical — horizontal wear surface. Work stain into grain. No drips on deck floor or siding.

tasks.name: Spindle Stain — Spray Application
tasks.description: Spray stain onto spindles/balusters with airless at low pressure. Use cardboard shield behind spindles to contain overspray. Follow with detail brush to work stain into all faces and joints. Efficient for large spindle counts (>30).

quality_notes.all: Shield behind spindles to contain overspray. Brush all faces after spray — spray alone misses inner faces. Turned spindles require extra brush attention in grooves.

tasks.name: Spindle Stain — Brush Application
tasks.description: Apply stain to individual spindles/balusters by brush. 2-3 inch detail brush. All 4 sides plus top/bottom joints. Turned spindles: work stain into turned profiles. High labor intensity — primary bottleneck in railing scope.

quality_notes.all: All 4 faces plus top/bottom joints. Turned spindles: wrap brush around profile, work into grooves. No drips — wipe excess from bottom of spindle. ~2-3 min per square spindle, 4-5 min per turned spindle.

tasks.name: Railing Stain — Second Coat
tasks.description: Apply second coat of stain to railing system. Required for semi_solid and solid_stain coating types. Same application method as coat 1. Allow recoat time per product TDS.

quality_notes.all: Same method as coat 1. Even coverage on all railing faces. Verify recoat time.

tasks.name: Spindle Stain — Second Coat
tasks.description: Apply second coat of stain to spindles/balusters. Required for semi_solid and solid_stain coating types. Same method as coat 1.

quality_notes.all: Same method as coat 1. All faces. Turned spindle grooves — verify full coverage.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Railing stain (spray_backbrush OR brush) -> Spindle stain (spray OR brush) -> Recoat time -> Railing coat 2 (conditional) -> Spindle coat 2 (conditional). Stain railings AFTER floor to avoid drips on finished floor — OR mask floor at railing base.

sop_modules.name: Deck Stair Stain Application
sop_modules.description: Apply stain to deck stair steps (tread + riser per step). Brush application only — no spray on stairs (tight geometry, adjacent surfaces, safety). Alternating step pattern: stain every other step, allow to dry, then stain remaining steps to maintain access. Second coat conditional on coating_type.

tasks.name: Stair Step Stain — Brush Application
tasks.description: Apply stain to deck stair steps by brush. Each step = tread top + riser face + stringer edge. Use alternating step pattern: stain odd-numbered steps first, allow to set (30-60 min for penetrating, 2-4 hr for solid), then stain even-numbered steps. Includes end-grain sealing on cut stringer ends.

quality_notes.all: Alternating step pattern for access. End-grain on stringer cuts absorbs heavily — pre-seal end grain or apply extra stain to cut ends. Tread nosing is high-wear — ensure full stain penetration.

tasks.name: Stair Step Stain — Second Coat
tasks.description: Apply second coat of stain to deck stair steps. Required for semi_solid and solid_stain. Same alternating step pattern as coat 1. Allow recoat time per product TDS.

quality_notes.all: Same alternating pattern. Verify recoat time. Tread nosing — high-wear area, ensure full coverage.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Stain stairs LAST (after floor and railings) — stairs are the exit path. Alternating step pattern for continuous access. Coat 2 conditional on coating_type.

sop_modules.name: Deck Cleanup & Final Inspection
sop_modules.description: Final walkthrough inspection, touch-up defects, return deck furniture, remove all protection materials, clean tools and equipment.

tasks.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection
tasks.description: Walk entire deck surface and inspect all stained areas: floor field, railings, spindles, stairs. Check for holidays, missed spots, drips, lap marks, and uneven absorption. Inspect in natural daylight — overcast conditions best for revealing coverage defects on horizontal surfaces.

quality_notes.all: Inspect all stained surfaces. Check board-to-board color consistency. Verify railing and spindle coverage on all faces. Document any defects for touch-up.

tasks.name: Touch-Up Defects
tasks.description: Brush touch-up of defects found during final inspection. Focus on holidays, missed board edges, board gaps, and railing/spindle missed faces. For penetrating stains: touch-up blends well (stain absorbs into bare spots). For solid stain: touch-up must feather edges to avoid visible overlap.

quality_notes.all: Penetrating stain touch-up blends naturally. Solid stain touch-up: feather edges, work quickly to maintain wet edge with surrounding area. Fix all noted defects.

tasks.name: Return Deck Furniture
tasks.description: Return all deck furniture, planters, grills, and accessories to original positions. Verify stain is fully dry/set before placing furniture (check with finger press — no tackiness). Place furniture pads under legs to prevent stain marking during initial cure period.

quality_notes.all: Verify stain is set (no tackiness) before placing furniture. Furniture pads under legs recommended for first 7 days of cure. Return items to original positions per staging documentation.

tasks.name: Protection Material Removal
tasks.description: Remove all masking tape, plastic sheeting from siding, landscape tarps, hardscape covers, and fixture masking. Check for tape residue on siding. Inspect landscape for stain overspray or chemical runoff damage.

quality_notes.all: Remove ALL protection materials. Check siding for tape residue or stain splash. Inspect landscape below deck for chemical damage from wash/strip runoff. Clean any overspray from hardscape immediately.

tasks.name: Tool and Equipment Cleaning
tasks.description: Clean all brushes, pad applicators, roller covers, and airless sprayer (if used). Stain is harder on brushes than paint — flush thoroughly. Clean spray tips and filters. Dispose of used applicators. Collect all debris, cans, and materials.

quality_notes.all: Flush sprayer completely — stain residue hardens in pump and hoses. Clean brushes immediately — stain-saturated bristles cannot be recovered once dried. Dispose of stain-soaked rags safely (spontaneous combustion risk with oil-based stains — lay flat to dry or submerge in water).

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Final inspect -> Touch-up -> Furniture return (after stain is set) -> Protection teardown -> Tool cleaning -> Site debris cleanup.

round_configurations.name: Clear Sealer — 1 Coat
round_configurations.description: Single coat clear sealer application. No primer. No second coat standard (optional second coat at homeowner request).
round_configurations.notes: Clear sealer — single coat penetrating. No primer. No interstage. Simplest round configuration.

round_configurations.name: Semi-Transparent Stain — 1 Coat
round_configurations.description: Single coat semi-transparent penetrating stain. Professional standard default. No primer required.
round_configurations.notes: Semi-transparent — single coat standard for penetrating stain. Second coat optional (some products allow wet-on-wet second coat same day). No primer. No interstage.

round_configurations.name: Semi-Solid Stain — 2 Coats
round_configurations.description: Two-coat semi-solid penetrating stain system. Second coat required for full opacity and durability.
round_configurations.notes: Semi-solid — 2 coats required. No formal interstage (penetrating stain absorbs, no intercoat sanding). Recoat time per TDS between coats.

round_configurations.name: Solid Stain — 2 Coats
round_configurations.description: Two-coat solid (film-forming) stain system. Second coat mandatory for film build and durability on horizontal wear surfaces. DELAMINATION RISK on horizontal surfaces — document risk acknowledgment.
round_configurations.notes: Solid stain — 2 coats mandatory. Film-forming coating on horizontal surface = delamination risk. Must document risk with homeowner. No formal interstage — allow full dry between coats per TDS (typically 4-24 hr depending on product and conditions).

key_deck_rules_enforced: Spray on deck stain = ALWAYS spray_backbrush (spray-only PROHIBITED). Back-brushing forces penetrating stain into wood grain.
Moisture test MC <=15% is hard stop — do not stain.
PT pine seasoning minimum 3 months — hard stop if <3 months from install.
Chemical restoration sequence is strict: strip -> dwell -> scrub -> rinse -> brighten -> dwell -> rinse -> 24-48 hr dry.
Cedar/redwood auto-add brightener (tannin management) even without full chemical strip.
Stair application is always brush — no spray on stairs (safety, geometry).
Second coat required for semi_solid and solid_stain coating types.
Solid stain on horizontal deck = DELAMINATION RISK — must document risk acknowledgment.
Alternating step pattern for stairs — stain every other step for continuous access.
24-48 hr dry time after pressure wash or chemical restoration before staining.

assumptions.value: Spray on deck stain = auto-add back-brush. Spray-only is PROHIBITED for penetrating stains.
assumptions.source: Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine.md Part A §6: Back-brushing forces stain into wood grain pores — spray alone does not achieve adequate penetration on wood.
assumptions.note: Explicit doctrine. Parallel to masonry spray_backroll requirement but with brush instead of roller.

assumptions.value: MC <=15% for deck wood (vs <=12% for masonry)
assumptions.source: Exterior_Decks_Horizontal_Wood_Doctrine.md §3: Wood substrate MC threshold 15% for exterior stain application.
assumptions.note: Wood has higher acceptable MC than masonry. 15% is the standard field threshold for exterior wood staining.

assumptions.value: Chemical restoration effectively requires a separate mobilization day (24-48 hr dry time after final rinse)
assumptions.source: Exterior_Decks_Horizontal_Wood_Doctrine.md §4: Chemical restoration protocol requires full drying period before stain application.
assumptions.note: Estimation Engineer must account for 2-day minimum project duration when wood_condition = weathered. Day 1: chemical restore. Day 2+: stain application.

assumptions.value: Solid stain on horizontal deck surfaces has inherent delamination risk — film-forming coating on high-wear horizontal surface exposed to UV and moisture
assumptions.source: Exterior_Decks_Horizontal_Wood_Doctrine.md §5: Solid stain failure mode is delamination/peeling (film-forming) vs penetrating stain failure mode is fading/erosion.
assumptions.note: Risk documentation is a business requirement, not a technical SOP task. Flag for project documentation template.

assumptions.value: Cedar and redwood substrates should receive oxalic acid brightener treatment even when not doing full chemical strip — tannin management
assumptions.source: Exterior_Decks_Horizontal_Wood_Doctrine.md §3: Cedar/redwood tannin deposits cause bleed-through and interfere with stain absorption.
assumptions.note: Doctrine covers tannin management but does not explicitly mandate standalone brightener for new cedar/redwood. Derived from field practice: oxalic acid brightener on new cedar/redwood prevents tannin bleed-through under semi-transparent stain.

assumptions.value: Mildew treatment is a site-condition-gated task (include_when mildew_present)
assumptions.source: Site_Condition_Vocabulary_Reference.md; field practice for deck maintenance
assumptions.note: Mildew is common on deck wood but not formally defined as site_condition_id in current vocabulary. Using 'mildew_present' with values light/moderate/severe. Flag for Site_Condition_Vocabulary addition.

exclusions.reason: Composite decking (Trex, TimberTech, etc.) is explicitly excluded from this spec. Composite substrates have fundamentally different prep, product, and application requirements. Separate spec family would be needed.

No primer module. Penetrating stains (clear, semi-transparent, semi-solid) do not use primer. Solid stain on cedar/redwood may require tannin-blocking primer as edge case — handled as specialty consumable, not a full module.
exclusions.source: resolution.json phase prohibited: prime; research.json RF-001

exclusions.reason: No interstage module. Penetrating stains absorb into wood — no intercoat sanding needed. Solid stain recoat follows product TDS timing only, no surface prep between coats.
This spec uses coating_type as primary configuration dimension instead of quality_tier. Task classifications use ct_ prefix (coating_type) instead of qt_ prefix (quality_tier) where applicable.
